claims.description: Source-artifact QA reproduced the real failure after all four migration replay assertions passed: pg_stat_activity still reported one backend at the original ten-second deadline, so teardown threw before DROP and preserved the scratch database. The focused non-DB regression models that exact ten-second linger and was observed red against the original timeout before turning green with the extended bounded drain window.

closePoolAndDropScratchDatabase ends the scratch pool, polls pg_stat_activity by the exact scratch database name until the backend count reaches zero, and only then issues a normal DROP DATABASE. A bounded timeout throws instead of escalating to FORCE.

The profiles-dropped migration replay suite's afterAll now delegates teardown to the drain-aware helper; admin-pool shutdown and temporary migration-directory removal remain protected by finally blocks.

Scratch isolation remains database-name scoped: the helper queries pg_stat_activity with the generated scratch database name as a parameter and drops that same quoted identifier. The default bounded drain window is thirty seconds, allowing the observed ten-second socket linger to resolve safely. An explicit short timeout test proves a genuinely persistent connection still throws and leaves the database intact rather than force-killing it.

The existing CI workflow runs the co-located integration glob containing the profiles-dropped suite against two disposable pgvector Postgres services (the required main lane and the flag-on diagnostic lane), providing two isolated real-database executions for the PR without using the shared staging endpoint.
